rationale:
RFC_029 §10.13 step 5 flips the resolver's whole-tree search from "conflicting candidates resolve to the stable shallowest winner + WARN" to "conflicting candidates resolve to NOTHING". Its precondition: "zero conflict WARNs observed over the window, OR every observed field/caller pair given an explicit mapping first." This is the second field/caller pair I have dispositioned toward that precondition (the first was migration 512, tool-generator/reason, APPROVED and applied 2026-08-20).

page-build-handler/`page_type` reawakened during my previous session: quiet since 08-18, then 3 rows in one 08-20 evening window. `plan_sections` declares `page_type` Optional and page-build-handler's `plan_sections` step does not wire it, so the search collects every `page_type` in the tree (the page's own record under two aliases, plus 28 sibling pages' types from the site's page list) and hands over the shallowest — `load_page_record.page_type`, in all 40 rows logged since 08-16.

This is the OPPOSITE disposition from 512. There, absence was the correct outcome and I declared the field out of the search entirely. Here the guessed value is RIGHT, not foreign: `load_page_record` is the step that loads THIS page's own record, and `page_record` (its own output_field alias) is mechanically the same value under a second key — 13/13 orchestrations with either populated show them agreeing exactly, because they are two names for one write, not two independent sources. So the fix is to WIRE the field explicitly (Strategy 0 resolves it directly, the step-1 prune then removes it from what the search is asked for), matching the sibling wire already on this exact step: `"page_name": "page_record.name"` becomes precedent for `"page_type": "page_record.page_type"`.

Why this one is riskier to leave unwired than 512's `reason` was: an absent `page_type` is NOT harmless here. plan_sections_action.go:972-973 falls back to the PAGE NAME when page_type is empty (`if pageType == "" { pageType = pageName }`), feeding a component-selector relevance scorer a slug where it expects a type. If step 5 ships before this pair is dispositioned, the flip would silently degrade that scoring for every page-build-handler run — a real behaviour change, not an inert substitution. This migration prevents that outcome from ever being reachable, rather than merely documenting it.

plan.summary: Wire page-build-handler's plan_sections step to read page_type from page_record.page_type (matching the sibling page_name wire already on the step), so the whole-tree search stops being the only source for a field whose absence would silently degrade the component selector's relevance scoring. Config-only migration + rollback sidecar; the guessed value is measurably correct today, so this is an explicit-wire disposition, not an absence disposition (contrast migration 512).

edits.rationale: Adds page_type = "page_record.page_type" to page-build-handler's plan_sections step, matching the sibling page_name = "page_record.name" wire already on the same step. Strategy 0 then resolves it directly and the live step-1 prune removes it from what Strategy 1/2 request, so the whole-tree search is never reached for this field on this step. Guarded to refuse if the step has been restructured, if page_type is already wired (another session), or if the sibling page_name convention has changed (matching a changed convention blindly would introduce a mismatch, not fix one). VERIFY is a DO/RAISE block asserting the exact value, asserting all five pre-existing keys survived jsonb_set, and a RECURSIVE in-transaction negative control (this lane's own twice-bitten top-level-jsonb_each trap) that the only other live caller of plan_sections, page-content-writer, is untouched — it has no load_page_record/page_record step at all, so this wire would be meaningless there.
edits.sketch: UPDATE agent_definitions SET default_config = jsonb_set(default_config, '{workflow,steps,plan_sections,config,page_type}', '"page_record.page_type"'::jsonb, true) WHERE type='page-build-handler' AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL;

edits.rationale: Removes the wire with `#-`, refusing if page_type is absent (not applied) or is NOT the exact value 514 wrote (another session re-pointed it on purpose). Names the observable that would justify running it: the component selector's relevance scoring regressing for a page whose page_record.page_type is genuinely absent but some other tree location held a valid value the search would have found — check collected_data->'page_record'->>'page_type' on the failing run before blaming this file.
edits.sketch: default_config #- '{workflow,steps,plan_sections,config,page_type}', then assert absence AND that the neighbouring page_name key was not taken with it.

grounded_in: plan_sections_action.go:54 — Optional includes page_type; :968-973 — 'site_type and page_type for the component selector fallback path. If not provided (existing workflows), the selector still works — it just scores without site/page type relevance bonuses.' pageType := inputs.Get("page_type"); if pageType == "" { pageType = pageName }.

The live plan_sections step on page-build-handler, read from agent_definitions 2026-08-21: {site_id: site_record.site_id, sections: spec_sections.sections, page_name: page_record.name, error_step: mark_item_failed, work_item_id: input_data.work_item_id, section_facts: spec_sections.section_facts} — no page_type wire, and page_name already uses the page_record.* convention this migration extends.

load_page_record step's output_field is page_record (agent_definitions workflow.steps.load_page_record.output_field), so load_page_record.page_type and page_record.page_type are two keys naming ONE written value, not independent sources.

Agreement measurement 2026-08-21: of 31 recent page-build-handler orchestrations, 18 have both load_page_record and page_record page_type NULL (outside this workflow run's scope at read time) and the remaining 13 agree exactly, 13/13 — SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE collected_data->'load_page_record'->>'page_type' = collected_data->'page_record'->>'page_type') FROM orchestration_states WHERE owner_agent_type='page-build-handler'.

Full conflict history 2026-08-21: 40 RESOLVER_CONFLICTING_CANDIDATES rows for page-build-handler/page_type since 2026-08-16, winner = load_page_record.page_type in ALL 40, most recent three at 2026-08-20 15:03/15:07/15:11Z after two quiet days — the class is live, not historical.

Fleet-wide callers of plan_sections, 2026-08-21: exactly two live steps — page-build-handler.plan_sections (this file) and page-content-writer.plan_sections, whose config wires site_id/sections/page_name from input_data.current_page.* and has NO load_page_record or page_record step in its 14-step workflow, so it carries no page_type candidate at all — out of scope for this fix, confirmed by a recursive (sub_workflow-safe) census.

RFC_029 §9 D2's precondition, quoted verbatim from findFieldRecursive's own comment (unified_extractor.go): 'zero conflict WARNs observed over the window, or every observed field/caller pair given an explicit mapping first.'
The step-1 prune (live v1.0.1310), action_inputs.go:767-781: a Strategy-0-resolved field is removed from what Strategy 1/2 request, so a wired page_type is never handed to the whole-tree search.

Direct precedent in this same RFC: migration 512 (tool-generator/reason, APPROVED corr 2bd7fb37-cac2-409a-8452-50a7ed933467, applied 2026-08-20) used the identical guard/VERIFY/recursive-negative-control shape for the same class of defect on a different field/caller pair — there the disposition was declared ABSENCE; here it is an explicit WIRE, and the header states why the two pairs take opposite fixes.
plan.risks:
1. THIS PAIR TAKES THE OPPOSITE DISPOSITION FROM MY OWN PRECEDENT (512), AND THAT IS DELIBERATE, NOT AN INCONSISTENCY. 512 declared reason ABSENT because absence was the desired outcome there. Here I am WIRING a value because the guessed value is measurably correct and losing it would be a real regression (the page-name fallback at plan_sections_action.go:973). A reviewer comparing the two migrations should expect different shapes for that reason, not treat the difference as an error in one of them.

2. THE AGREEMENT MEASUREMENT IS SAMPLED, NOT EXHAUSTIVE. 13/13 agreement is against orchestration_states' ~24h retention window, not the field's full history. The full agent_error_log conflict history (40/40 rows won by load_page_record.page_type since 08-16) is the stronger, longer-window evidence, and I am citing both rather than relying on the smaller sample alone. The disconfirming observation would be any run where page_record.page_type and load_page_record.page_type genuinely diverge — I have not found one, but I have only checked the retained window.

3. I HAVE NOT VERIFIED THE MIGRATION'S EFFECT YET, BECAUSE I CANNOT: page-build-handler's demand is intermittent (78 runs/24h a day ago, near-zero in the hours right before this submission per the lane's own demand-control convention). I will bank a pre-apply baseline and state the detection floor explicitly in the commit and lane NOTES, the same discipline 512 used, rather than claim a fix before the class has had a chance to fire again.

4. THIS DISPOSITIONS ONE OF THE REMAINING LIVE PAIRS, NOT THE FLIP ITSELF. build-dispatch-loop/commit_sha remains blocked on the bugfix_315 lane's judgement (a CONTRIB is with them, unanswered as of this submission) and tool-generator/related_pages (bugs_open/330) is a different fix already scoped (absence is the desired outcome there too, but its resolver-scope candidate 2 is unbuilt and its own audit found 269/309 wire-pairs still unsampled fleet-wide). Nothing about this migration should be read as evidence the resolver is safe more broadly — the same permanent blind spot applies: a conflict row requires candidates to DIFFER, so an agreeing or single-candidate substitution elsewhere in the estate is invisible to this instrument regardless of this fix.

5. SITE_TYPE IS THE SAME SHAPE AND IS NOT TOUCHED HERE. plan_sections also declares site_type Optional and page-build-handler's plan_sections step wires neither field today. I have not measured whether site_type is silently substituting a value on this step (it produces no conflict rows, which per the instrument's known blind spot could mean either 'never asked' or 'resolves uniquely, unseen'). Scoped out of this submission deliberately; worth a follow-up measurement, not assumed safe by omission.
